definition: The average number of tokens needed per word (or per character) in a given language.
details: The average number of tokens needed per word (or per character) in a given language. High fertility means a language is "expensive": Arabic text on an English-centric tokenizer can cost 2-4x the tokens of equivalent English, directly inflating cost and shrinking effective context. A core metric for multilingual fairness.

explainer.lead: Tokenizer fertility measures how many tokens a tokenizer spends per word in a given language. It matters because high fertility makes a language more expensive to process and shrinks how much text fits in a context window.

tiers.eli5: Some languages get chopped into many little pieces by a model, like paying for a word one letter at a time, while others get whole words. The more pieces per word, the more you pay.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers compute fertility per target language to budget token costs and context sizing before shipping multilingual products. A common pitfall is tuning everything on English and only later discovering other languages cost several times more.
tiers.paperLevel: Fertility = tokens divided by words (or characters) over a corpus in a language. It is an average, so it hides variation across domains and scripts.

explainer.example: On an English-centric tokenizer, Arabic text can cost 2-4x the tokens of equivalent English, inflating cost and shrinking effective context.
